description:
Redwood Inference will ship an opt-in “Quantization Profile Library” that publishes per-model quantization profiles (e.g., fp16/bf16/int8/int4 variants, kernel+hardware constraints, calibration notes, expected speedup/cost deltas) and exposes route-level enablement controls so customers can selectively apply quantization to specific API routes/workloads.

Goals:
- Reduce inference unit cost (tokens/$) for supported models while maintaining customer-defined quality thresholds.
- Make quantization safer to adopt via route-level controls, canaries, and fast rollback.
- Standardize how Redwood creates, validates, versions, and distributes quantization profiles across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

Scope:
- Profile schema + storage in the model registry (versioned, signed, hardware-scoped, runtime-compatible).
- Runtime integration to fetch/resolve the right profile per request (model, hardware, sequence length regime) while respecting route-level policy.
- Control plane / config surface to enable/disable per route (and optional per-customer overrides), including API + Console exposure.
- Quality and performance validation pipeline (eval harness + perf suite), plus guardrails and monitoring.
- Documentation, rollout plan, and incident/runbook readiness.

Non-goals (initial release):
- Automatic “always-on” quantization for all customers.
- Arbitrary user-supplied quantization profiles (library is Redwood-published only in v1).
- Fully automated profile generation for every new model without human review.

Key stakeholders:
- Applied ML / Performance & Evals: Arjun Desai, Karthik Iyer, Jonas Weber (profile methodology, quality gates).
- Serving Runtime: Mateo Alvarez, Hiro Tanaka, Sofia Ivanova (runtime execution + kernel compatibility).
- Smart Routing / Platform: Mina Haddad, Ravi Menon (policy evaluation, route controls, safe fallback).
- Telemetry/Billing Hooks: Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman, Cole Summers (cost attribution, monitoring).
- Product: Aditya Rao (Optimize) + Nikhil Sharma (Hosted API) (PRD, packaging, launch criteria).
- SRE: eng-sre team (canary, rollback, incident response readiness).

Proposed timeline (10–12 weeks):
1) Weeks 1–2: PRD + design spec + schema/ADR decisions; choose initial model set and supported hardware.
2) Weeks 3–6: Implement model-registry artifacts + runtime resolution + route policy controls behind feature flags.
3) Weeks 5–8: Build validation pipeline (perf + evals), telemetry, dashboards, and rollback tooling.
4) Weeks 9–10: Private/Dedicated compatibility testing; docs + SDK guidance.
5) Weeks 11–12: Limited beta (opt-in), expand supported models, GA decision with quality/cost KPIs.

Constraints / risks:
- Quality regressions can be workload-specific; must ship conservative defaults, route-level canaries, and automated rollback signals.
- Hardware and kernel compatibility matrix is complex; profiles must be explicitly scoped and validated.
- Operational safety: config changes must be auditable and reversible; must not break billing attribution or routing fallbacks.

files.description: High-level overview of the opt-in quantization profile library: what a profile is, supported model families, versioning strategy, ownership, and how profiles are consumed by runtime + routing.
Specification of the quantization profile schema (fields, required metadata, hardware scoping, kernel constraints), semantic versioning rules, and backward/forward compatibility expectations.
Quality gate criteria and methodology: prompt sets, regression thresholds, safety checks, and approval workflow for publishing a profile to the library.
Plan to expand prompt-set coverage specifically for quantization evaluation (edge-case prompts, long context, tool-calling/JSON mode), including gaps and priority additions.
How eval-harness runs compare baseline vs quantized variants, reporting format, statistical tests, and how results attach to profile publish PRs.
Runtime design notes: profile lookup flow, caching of profile artifacts, compatibility checks, and the decision path between baseline kernels vs quantized kernels.
Perf benchmark plan for quantization profiles: datasets, load shapes, sequence length distributions, p50/p95 targets, and how results are tracked across GPUs/regions.
Platform/control-plane documentation for route-level quantization enablement: config model, precedence (org/customer/route), auditing, and interaction with routing/fallback.
ADR capturing why quantization is opt-in, why controls are route-scoped (vs model-scoped only), and the chosen rollout/rollback model.
API conventions for exposing quantization configuration (request headers vs route config, error semantics, validation responses, and deprecation policy).
Company-wide performance/quality acceptance thresholds for publishing profiles (minimum cost/latency improvement, max quality regression) and how exceptions are handled.
Operational runbook: detection signals, disabling a profile per route/customer, reverting to baseline, cache flush steps, and post-rollback validation.
Threat model for profile distribution and activation: artifact integrity, signing/verification, tampering risks, auditability, and least-privilege for publish permissions.
PRD covering customer problems, goals/non-goals, target personas, MVP scope, success metrics (cost savings, adoption, regression rate), and launch requirements.
Cross-functional design spec: user flows (Console + API), route-level toggles, canary settings, audit log entries, and interaction with rollouts/fallback policies.
Draft release notes for beta: supported models, how to opt in, known limitations, monitoring guidance, and support contacts.

Engineering issue: runtime fetch + caching of profiles, compatibility checks (GPU arch, kernels), and safe fallback to baseline.
Engineering issue: add route-level enablement to policy evaluation, precedence rules, and integration tests with routing/fallback.
Engineering issue: ensure token-level cost/latency attribution correctly tags quantized vs baseline execution and feeds Console dashboards.
Engineering issue: eval harness runner for baseline vs quantized comparisons; store results and link to profile publish workflow.
Engineering issue: canary rollout support, regression detection signals, and automatic disable/rollback hooks.
Engineering issue: update developer docs and SDK docs to explain route-level config, headers/params (if any), and troubleshooting steps.
